page: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance configured within a shared CPU infrastructure. It is powered by the Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 Broadwell processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 16 virtual CPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, alongside 40 MB of Level 3 cache. Memory capacity is set at 64.0 GB, maintaining a conventional 4:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration does not include bundled local disk storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and it provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate solid multi-threaded processing balanced against modest single-core execution capabilities. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves an average multi-core score of 12880.15, contrasted by a bottom-decile single-core score of 941.59. PassMark testing reflects a similar profile with an overall CPU score of 15708.54, accompanied by steady database operation metrics of 3535.53. In data handling and serving, the instance sustains 13.62 million Redis SET operations per second and 12.25 GB/sec static web throughput. Single-threaded compression is weak, yielding 21.23 GB/sec in gzip, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 53.85 GB/sec. Large-block memory bandwidth tests show 52.57 GB/sec read and 30.53 GB/sec write speeds.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.mn4.4xlarge lies in its older microarchitecture and shared core model, which limits single-threaded speed and lightweight machine learning inference on larger models. However, the high core density and balanced 64 GB RAM profile offer cost-efficient scalability for scale-out applications that do not depend on dedicated compute cycles. Best-fit deployments include multi-threaded batch jobs, web application serving pools, background worker queues, and caching services with moderate networking requirements.
